chunks: My father and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Abi 'Abdillah Al-Jamurani Al-Razi, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim Abi 'Ali, from Al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Jabir Al-Ju'fi, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Al-Mufaddal, as part of a long hadith about the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'Then you proceed to your prayer, and for you, for every Rak'ah you bow in prostration next to him, is the reward of one who performed one thousand Hajj, one thousand 'Umrah, freed one thousand slaves, and stood in the way of Allah one thousand times with a Messenger Prophet.' And he mentioned the hadith.

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Way of Allah (in the path of God)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for praying near the grave of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam Al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) declaration that each Rak'ah offered at the shrine of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) carries the reward of a thousand Hajj, a thousand Umrah, freeing a thousand slaves, and standing with a Messenger of God. This hadith underscores the theological concept of the Imām al-Zamanah (a.s.) as a locus of divine grace, where acts of worship performed in proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt are exponentially multiplied. It highlights the unique status of the shrines as spiritual centers that amplify the merit of both obligatory and voluntary prayers.
